yt_1.title: Most Small Firms Lose 30-40% of Enquiries (Here's How to Stop It)
yt_1.narration: I'm Andy Norman, founder of Antek Automation. Here's a number most owners find hard to believe until they check it. Most small firms lose thirty to forty per cent of their enquiries, simply because nobody was free to answer the phone. It's rarely one big failure. It's a hundred small ones. The phone rings during a client meeting. A call lands while reception is already on another line. Someone tries at six pm, when the office has closed. Each one feels minor. Added up across a month, it's a serious chunk of revenue walking out the door. And here's the sting. You paid to make most of those phones ring. The advertising, the website, the local ranking. So a missed call is paying for that lead twice, and still losing it. Start by knowing your own number. For one week, log every call that goes unanswered or to voicemail. Then multiply by the value of an average client. That figure is what the gap is costing you right now. Most owners are genuinely shocked when they see it. Then they do something about it. If you want to catch the callers you're missing and turn them into booked work, take a look at antek automation dot com.

yt_2.title: The Three Bosses of Local SEO Every UK Service Business Must Know
yt_2.narration: I'm Andy Norman from Antek Automation. Getting your business found online isn't one job. It's keeping three bosses happy at the same time. Ignore one and your rankings slip. Ignore two and you become invisible. Ignore all three and you're handing customers to your competitors. Boss one is Google's algorithm. That means a website that loads fast and works on a phone, plus a properly filled-in Google Business Profile with your real services and the areas you cover. None of it glamorous, all of it non-negotiable. Boss two is your customers. They don't search like a textbook. Nobody types comprehensive accountancy solutions. They type accountant near me, or emergency plumber, at eleven pm. So write for the words they actually use, and prove you know the local area. Boss three is your competitors. Ranking is relative. You don't need to be perfect. You need to be clearly better than the other firms chasing the same local searches. The trap is treating these as three separate jobs. The businesses that dominate local search keep all three happy with the same piece of content. If you want help getting found, take a look at antek automation dot com.

yt_3.title: What a Full-Time Receptionist Really Costs a Small Firm
yt_3.narration: I'm Andy Norman, founder of Antek Automation. Let's talk about a number most small firms never actually work out. A full-time receptionist costs between twenty and twenty-eight thousand pounds a year. Then add holiday cover, sick leave, and training on top. For a lot of accountancy practices, surveyors and small firms, that's a serious commitment. So the phone gets shared around the team, and calls get missed during meetings, lunch, and the school run. Here's the part that gets ignored. Even with a receptionist, most small businesses still lose thirty to forty per cent of their enquiries, because nobody was free to answer. That's not a problem you fix by working harder. It's a coverage problem. A twenty-four seven answering service catches every caller, answers the common questions, and books the appointment. For a fraction of a salary, and without a single day off. The point isn't to replace your team. It's to cover the calls they physically can't take. Work out your own number. personal_3.title: What Happens When Your Phone Rings After Hours (4-Step Process)
personal_3.narration: I'm Andy Norman, founder of Antek Automation. Someone asked me last week what actually happens when a call comes in after hours. Here's the honest step by step. Four steps, every time. First, it qualifies the enquiry by asking the questions that actually matter for that type of call. Second, it checks a live calendar and books directly if a slot's free. Third, if it's flagged urgent, like a burst pipe, it escalates straight to a named on-call person. Fourth, if it's none of the above, full contact and enquiry details get captured properly, ready for the morning. A burst pipe gets flagged urgent and escalated. A quote request waits politely until morning, booked in and logged. A Saturday viewing gets booked there and then, instead of leaving a voicemail nobody checks until Monday. The call gets answered every time, not just when someone happens to be free. It's the same four-step process for property clients and trades clients, just adjusted to each industry's own triage rules. If you want every call answered properly, day or night, take a look at antek automation dot com.

personal_7.title: The 5-Step Process Behind a Proper Custom AI Build
personal_7.narration: I'm Andy Norman, founder of Antek Automation. Most SMB owners looking into this have already tried a chatbot plugin and found it too generic to actually help. Here's why. Generic tools handle the easy eighty per cent of enquiries fine, and fail on the twenty per cent that needs real business logic. Checking actual availability. Applying your specific qualification criteria. Escalating to the right named person. A proper build follows five steps every time. Needs analysis, understanding your call volume and where leads currently get lost. Use-case mapping, turning that into specific scenarios. System design, deciding which platform and logic handles each one. Integration and testing, against your real telephony and CRM data. Then handover. For a trades business that might mean a voice agent that asks different diagnostic questions for a boiler breakdown versus a blocked drain. For professional services it might mean triaging enquiries by service line before a human ever sees them. The output looks different every time, because the business is different every time. That's the whole point of custom over generic. If you want a system built around how your business actually works, take a look at antek automation dot com.

Sounds like pure tech news. It isn't, if you're running a voice agent or intake automation. Here's why. If you're running a single chatbot, model pricing barely registers. If you're handling dozens or hundreds of calls a day, the maths changes fast. Every call your system handles costs money to process, interpret and respond to in real time. A model that handles more complex reasoning without jumping to premium pricing means you can automate more sophisticated tasks without your costs spiralling. Better reasoning shows up in fewer moments where the AI has to punt to a human. Better lead qualification before anything reaches your desk. More accurate appointment booking, because it actually understands scheduling conflicts. You don't need to follow every model release yourself. But the businesses whose vendors do, and who test and roll these updates in properly, end up with systems that sound more natural and cost less to run. That gap compounds.
